rics.description: ADP National Employment - Actual, Absolute change
rics.meaning: Absolute period-over-period change in ADP private-sector employment (national region).
rics.how_to_use: ADP private-payrolls release, two days before BLS NFP. Methodology change in 2022 makes ADP a less-reliable NFP predictor than it once was. Useful as a sectoral cross-check but not the headline.

rics.description: Labour Market n.i.e, ADP total nonfarm private employment (estimate)
rics.meaning: ADP private-sector employment estimate — released two days BEFORE the official BLS NFP. Based on ADP's payroll-processing client base.
rics.how_to_use: Methodology overhaul in 2022 made ADP a less-reliable NFP predictor. Use as a sectoral cross-check, not as a leading indicator of the BLS print. ADP captures small business better than BLS; BLS captures large + government better.

rics.meaning: Total nonfarm payroll employment level. The headline US 'jobs number' from the BLS establishment survey, released first Friday each month.
rics.how_to_use: Single most market-moving US data release. Watch (a) MoM change vs consensus, (b) prior-month revisions (often +/-50k swings), (c) sectoral breakdown (private services vs goods vs government), (d) hours-worked + average earnings released alongside. Pair with U-3 from the household survey for full picture.

rics.meaning: Total private-sector nonfarm payroll employment — excludes government workers. The cyclical part of NFP.
rics.how_to_use: Stripping out government employment (which is policy-driven, not cyclical) gives a cleaner read on private-sector hiring. Government swing months (e.g., census hiring/layoff) make headline NFP misleading; private payrolls are what the Fed really watches.

rics.description: Labour Market n.i.e, JOLTS Job Openings
rics.meaning: JOLTS Job Openings — total US job postings at the end of each month. BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, released ~6 weeks lagged.
rics.how_to_use: Openings/unemployed ratio (V/U) is the Fed's preferred labor-tightness gauge. V/U > 1.5 = very tight; V/U < 1.0 = loose. Crashed from 2.0 in 2022 toward 1.0 in 2024 — Fed's 'soft landing' is partly built on this falling without UR rising.

rics.description: Labour Market n.i.e, JOLTS, Nonfarm, Hires
rics.meaning: Level of a JOLTS measure — BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey, monthly. Job openings = posted vacancies; hires = new starts; quits = voluntary departures; separations = total departures.
rics.how_to_use: Quits rate is the cleanest worker-confidence gauge — high quits = workers confident they can find better jobs. Openings/unemployed ratio (V/U) was Fed's preferred labor-tightness gauge during 2022-23 wage-spiral concerns.

rics.description: Labour Market n.i.e, JOLTS, Nonfarm, Quits
rics.meaning: JOLTS Quits — voluntary departures. The cleanest worker-confidence gauge: high quits = workers confident they can find better jobs.
rics.how_to_use: Leads wage growth by 3-6 months (aUSEARNH/A YoY). 'Great Resignation' peak in 2022 (4.5M+/mo) faded by 2024. Quits below pre-pandemic baseline = workers locked in, wage growth moderating.
